top_story.headline: Iowa House challenger's campaign says outside actors diverted or tried to divert payments, including a $48,568 invoice swap
top_story.dek: Sarah for Iowa told the FEC on October 15 that two vendor payments were hit by unauthorized activity by an external actor, with police reports filed.
paragraphs: Sarah for Iowa, the committee of Democratic House challenger Sarah Trone Garriott, filed a Form 99 on October 15 describing two incidents. On August 6 it started a $48,568.16 ACH payment to a vendor, and 'an external actor altered the invoice in an attempt to redirect the payment to another bank account.' The committee says it found the problem on August 8, got a police report, and alerted the recipient bank, which flagged the transfer. The money was never deposited in the unknown account and was returned in full on August 10. The vendor was paid by check on August 13. Filing.

The second incident surfaced on October 8, when a vendor resubmitted a $15,000 invoice the committee believed it had paid on June 16. The committee says that earlier transaction was also unauthorized. It notified police the same day and amended its July Quarterly Report to disclose the transaction. It also reported the $15,000 as debt on its October Quarterly Report and paid the vendor in full on October 14. The filing, signed by treasurer Theresa Kehoe, says no one associated with the committee was involved and that it found no other unauthorized transactions. The committee says its Pre-General Report will disclose the vendor payment.

Two other filings from the same quarterly-deadline cycle are worth a look. AFC Victory Fund says a $600,000 loan from American Federation for Children, Inc. was forgiven effective August 25 and converted to a contribution. The attached memo is undated and unsigned, and it says campaign-finance counsel should confirm the conversion is permissible before it is relied on. Filing. Separately, the FEC sent Jo Jorgensen a disavowal notice saying a committee called Jo Jorgensen for President Exploratory Committee appears to have taken in or spent more than $5,000 for a 2028 candidacy. She has 35 days to disavow or file a Statement of Candidacy. Notice.

sections.headline: Excessive-contribution RFAIs for Miller-Meeks and Van Hollen; three members correct the record by Form 99
paragraphs: Seven filings are tagged to sitting lawmakers: three RFAIs (two for one committee), three Form 99 explanations and one termination approval. The two Miller-Meeks for Congress letters, received the same day, are the heaviest, with excessive contributions, post-primary primary-designated money and wrong cycle-to-date totals.

items: Miller-Meeks for Congress — Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA), RFAI received 10/15 on the amended 12 Day Pre-Primary Report (4/1–5/13/2026, received 7/7/2026): FEC says the report discloses activity outside its coverage dates and that Column B cycle-to-date totals on Lines 11(a)(i), 11(a)(ii), 11(a)(iii) and 11(c) appear incorrect. Response due 11/19. Filing.

Miller-Meeks for Congress — Miller-Meeks (R-IA), second RFAI received 10/15 on the July Quarterly Report (5/14–6/30/2026), four items: (1) contributions over the per-election limit, with FEC noting the committee's explanation of corrective action but saying some have still not been refunded, redesignated or reattributed within 60 days; (2) another set of excessive contributions that the committee has refunded, though FEC says some were not refunded within 60 days; (3) contributions received after the primary but designated for it, allowed only up to net debts outstanding; (4) Column B totals on Lines 7(a), 7(c), 17 and 22 that appear wrong. The treasurer is Thomas Datwyler. Response due 11/19. Filing.

Van Hollen for Senate — Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), RFAI received 10/14 on the July Quarterly Report (4/1–6/30/2026), two items: contributions that appear to exceed the $3,500 per-election individual limit, which must be refunded, redesignated or reattributed within 60 days, and Schedule A entries on Line 11(a)(i) without proper election designations (FEC asks the committee to clarify the 'P2026' designation). Treasurer Janica Kyriacopoulos. Response due 11/18. Filing.

Frelinghuysen for Congress — Rodney P. Frelinghuysen (R-NJ, tagged as a sitting lawmaker), Form 99 received 10/14 answering an RFAI: the committee says it will keep using residual cash for 'ongoing campaign support of various political candidates and organizations' at federal, state and local levels and/or charities, that none will be converted to personal use, and that it will keep filing until the cash is fully disbursed or it terminates. Filing.

Lou Correa for Congress — Rep. J. Luis Correa (D-CA), Form 99 received 10/15: the committee's October 15 quarterly report noted two excessive contributions of $1,500 each, and refund checks for both were issued October 14. Filing.

Russ Fulcher for Idaho — Rep. Russ Fulcher (R-ID), Form 99 received 10/14: a contribution from the National Multifamily Housing Council And Real Estate Technology And Transformation Center PAC on the April 2026 Q1 report was entered as $1,000 but should have been $5,000, so it was understated by $4,000 until an amended Q1 report was filed 10/14; later reports were also amended. Signed by treasurer Julie Johnson. Filing.
Ben Cardin for Senate, Inc. — termination approval received 10/14, tagged as a sitting lawmaker (D-MD, Senate). Not read. Filing.

sections.headline: 63 RFAIs from other filers: a batch of unregistered-looking candidates, missing reports for a Mississippi challenger, and a cluster of party-committee allocation questions
paragraphs: Beyond the lawmakers, 60 RFAIs arrived (25 to candidates or their committees, 35 to PACs and party committees). Most are standard types: wrong cash balances, bad Column B totals, vague disbursement purposes, excessive contributions and Schedule H4 allocation problems. Three letters carry the red-flag keyword 'fraud', but it comes only from the boilerplate 18 U.S.C. § 1001 warning in FEC Form 1 and Form 2 verification letters (to Simeon B. Kedikoglou and to two committees); none alleges fraud.

Four RFAIs went to Mark for Nebraska and three to Friends of Jon Thorp (plus a termination-report RFAI); the Thorp committee is the likeliest to be unwinding. Sawyer Walters' committee was told FEC has no April or July quarterly report on file.

items: Senate candidate Simeon B. Without a response in 35 days FEC will move his Form 2 and related filings to its unverified-filings database. The 'fraud' keyword is the standard 18 U.S.C. § 1001 warning. Due 11/18. Filing.

Treasurer is Dickie Corder. Filing.

sections.headline: 76 Form 99s: loan forgiveness of $494,000 to $691,000, a rescinded-registration request and a flood of 'below the threshold' statements
paragraphs: Quarterly-deadline week produced 76 non-lawmaker Form 99s (including three duplicate postings). More than 30 are statements that the committee has not reached the $5,000 reporting threshold, and nine arrived with a blank text field. Substantive ones include three candidate or lender loan forgiveness filings and replies to RFAIs.

Two committees say their termination is waiting on FEC action: Patriot Freedom PAC Inc and Principled Veterans Fund each cite a pending quorum of commissioners. Patrick Krason signed filings for Patriot Freedom PAC, Veterans Movement PAC and Natalie Rivera for US Senate 2026.

items: Jo Jorgensen (Libertarian, presidential), FEC disavowal notice received 10/15: FEC says Jo Jorgensen for President Exploratory Committee has filed reports and appears to have received or spent over $5,000 for her '2028 candidacy'; she has 35 days to disavow in writing or file a Form 2. Due 11/19. Notice.

AFC Victory Fund (type O), loan forgiveness, received 10/15: on February 6, 2026 it borrowed $600,000 from American Federation for Children, Inc. (interest-free, unsecured, no repayment date); effective August 25 the lender forgave the balance and converted it into a contribution. The attached memo by Jennifer Miller, the lender's treasurer, has a blank signature date and says counsel should confirm the conversion is permissible. Filing.

Christi Jacobsen for Congress (Republican Christi Jacobsen, open-seat House race in Montana), loan forgiveness, received 10/15: a letter dated October 9 forgives all her loans and obligations to the committee, $494,277.06. Filing.

Jorge Martinez for Congress (Republican Jorge Martinez, House challenger, Florida), loan forgiveness, received 10/13: he forgave on 9/8/2026 loans of $250,000 (5/26), $250,000 (6/29) and $150,000 (8/10) plus the remaining $41,138.14 of a 7/29 loan, at least $691,138.14, reflected on the October quarterly. Treasurer is Joel Jukus. Filing.
Sarah for Iowa: reports two unauthorized payment incidents by an external actor (see Top Story). Filing.

Digital Ground Game (type N), received 10/14: says it is a 501(c)(4) that filed a Form 1 on 9/30/2026 'in error,' is not a political committee, and asks FEC to rescind the registration, terminate ID C00962670 and confirm no reports are due. Signed Bryce Peever, executive director. Filing.

Patriot Freedom PAC Inc (type V), three copies received 10/15: a statement dated 7/15/2026 'for the 2026 Q2 filing' says the committee filed its termination report 6/10/2025, is awaiting a quorum, has ceased operations and closed its bank account. Filing, duplicate, duplicate.

Principled Veterans Fund (PV Fund) (type O), received 10/15: says an FEC analyst told it termination approval is pending a quorum to certify a negotiated settlement agreement, so no further reports are required. Signed by treasurer Timothy Koch. Filing.

The Bench (type W), reply to a 9/9 letter on the July Quarterly, received 10/14: a 6/12/2026 transfer of $80,583.75 from the non-federal account included a $58,500 non-federal share for an expense paid 8/5/2026; the committee says an 'administrative error' sent funds early and it returned the $58,500 to the non-federal account on 10/1. It blames a software error for wrong H4 totals and filed an amendment. Signed by treasurer Christopher Koob. Filing.

Republican Party of Arkansas, reply to a 9/24 letter on the August Monthly, received 10/14: corrected H4 administrative totals in an amendment, and says a Catering Services payment was for state-level activity paid in error from the federal account; it asked the vendor for a refund. Filing.

Ohio Democratic Party - Federal, reply on the July Monthly, received 10/14: a contribution from DLZ Corp Infrastructure Advocacy Federal PAC was misdeposited in the federal account and refunded to the non-federal account, to appear on the M10 report; it says the 'Communications Consulting' payment was not for public communications referring to a clearly identified federal candidate. Filing.
